title: Controv. XV: Should the Reformed, by the rule of charity, tolerate Lutherans as brethren?
pass_a_gloss: Fifteenth head. On mutual tolerance among Evangelicals. Whether the Reformed, by the rule of charity, though they think otherwise than the Lutherans on the chapters above — the graver consequences of those chapters not standing in the way, because those consequences are not acknowledged by the Lutherans but rather rejected; both because the weight in other chapters is lighter if the state of the controversy is rightly explained, as in the chapter on the Holy Supper, and so on; and also because the principle and foundation of the faith common to Protestants has been retained, and idolatry and papal doctrine rejected — whether they are ready to tolerate the Lutherans as brethren and sharers of the same faith and salvation, and as members of the true Church, in a holy confederation of hearts and studies?
pass_b_english: Controv. XV. On mutual tolerance among Evangelicals.

By the rule of charity, should the Reformed — though they differ from the Lutherans on the chapters above — be ready to bear with them as brethren, sharers of the same faith and salvation, and members of the true church, in a holy bond of hearts and studies?

The graver consequences of those chapters need not block the way: the Lutherans neither own those consequences nor accept them. Other heads weigh less once the real state of the quarrel is set out fairly — as in the chapter on the Holy Supper. And both sides still keep the common Protestant principle and foundation of the faith, having rejected idolatry and papal doctrine.
source_text: XV. De Tolerantia mutua inter Evangelicos. An Reformati, ex canone charitatis, secùs sentientes in superioribus Capitibus Lutheranos, (nihil obstantibus istorum Capitum gravioribus consequentüs, sed ab his non agnitis, imò rejectis; tùm ob levius in aliis Capitibus momentum, si status Controversiae ritè explicetur, ut in Capite de S. Canâ, &c. tùm etiam ob retentum fidei principium ac fundamentum, Protestantibus commune, rejectamque Idololatriam, ac doctrinam Papalem) tolerare parati sint tanquam Fratres, & consortes ejusdem fidei ac salutis, ac membra verae Ecclesiae, sanctâ confederatione animorum, studiorumque?
notes: Controv. print pp. 75-76 / PDF ~176-177. Opening of De Tolerantia mutua (XV).
